inputs.resume_text:
VIKRAM SINGH RATHORE
PGP 2025-27, Indian Institute of Management Indore | vikram.rathore@iimidr.ac.in

EDUCATION
PGP, IIM Indore, 2025-27, CGPA 7.4/10 (Term 1-3)
B.Tech, Mechanical Engineering, Military College of Electronics and Mechanical Engineering (JNU), 2017, 7.9/10

WORK EXPERIENCE (60 months)
Indian Army, Corps of EME, Captain | Jun 2018 - May 2023
- Commanded a 120-member Light Repair Workshop supporting an armoured regiment in Rajasthan
- Cut average vehicle turnaround time from 9 days to 5 days by redesigning the spares indent cycle and setting up a forward spares cell
- Managed spares inventory worth INR 14 crore across 3 depots; brought audit discrepancies down to zero in two consecutive annual audits
- Led recovery of 22 vehicles during a flash flood exercise in Barmer with no casualties
Indian Army, Lieutenant | Jun 2017 - May 2018
- Officer-in-charge of a training cadre of 40 craftsmen
Career note: Jun 2023 - Jun 2025, prepared for CAT and worked as a volunteer instructor at a veterans' skilling centre in Jaipur

SUMMER INTERNSHIP
Tata Steel, Kalinganagar | Operations Intern | Apr - Jun 2026
- Built a criticality-based spares stocking model for 312 hot strip mill spares; projected INR 3.2 crore reduction in inventory holding with no rise in breakdown risk
- Mapped the breakdown-to-repair process across 4 departments and proposed a single work-order queue; adopted for the cold rolling mill pilot
- Received Pre-Placement Interview (PPI)

POSITIONS OF RESPONSIBILITY
- Member, Operations Club (OpsCom), IIM Indore: organised Supply Chain Summit with 9 industry speakers
- Sports Secretary, Officers' Mess, 2021-22

ACHIEVEMENTS
- Chief of Army Staff Commendation Card, 2022
- National finalist, Mahindra War Room 2025 (top 8 of 1,100 teams)

plan.warmup_question: Which part of your current MBA coursework has been most engaging so far?
plan.background_question: Walk me through your career so far, including your time preparing for CAT and what you have focused on since starting your MBA.

slots.core_question: I see you built a spares stocking model at Tata Steel. What problem were you trying to solve?
slots.intent_private: Needs the business context, Vikram's own analysis and decisions, how criticality and breakdown risk were assessed, and how the projected INR 3.2 crore saving was calculated.
likely_probes: Which decisions in the model were yours?
What did you compare the projected saving against?
What made you confident breakdown risk would not rise?

slots.core_question: At the Indian Army, how did you bring vehicle turnaround down from 9 days to 5 days?
slots.intent_private: Needs a specific operational story covering the bottleneck Vikram found, the changes he personally made to the spares process, stakeholder coordination, and how the turnaround figures were measured.
likely_probes: Which part of the process did you change first?
What did you decide not to change?
How were the 9-day and 5-day averages calculated?

slots.core_question: How would you set a stocking level for a spare whose demand is unpredictable but whose failure can stop production?
slots.intent_private: Needs an applied explanation of criticality, service levels, lead time, demand uncertainty, and holding-cost trade-offs, with a clear approach to validating the policy in operations.
likely_probes: Why would you use that approach over a simple average-demand calculation?
When might your approach create too much inventory?
How would you validate the policy using an example from your own work?

plan.plan_notes: The plan prioritizes the Tata Steel internship and the Army turnaround achievement because they provide the strongest evidence of supply-chain analysis and operational execution. A knowledge question tests inventory-policy judgment at full MBA depth; the resume otherwise offers unusually strong quantified leadership and logistics evidence, with no material gap or short-stint concern.
